title: Portland, Maine
description: Most populous city in Maine, United States
wiki_lead:
Portland is the most populous city in the U.S. state of Maine. Its population was 68,408 at the 2020 census and the Greater Portland metropolitan area has a population of approximately 550,000 people, the most populous metropolitan area in Maine. It is the county seat of Cumberland County. Historically tied to commercial shipping, the marine economy, and light industry, Portland's economy in the 21st century relies mostly on the service sector. The Port of Portland is the second-largest tonnage seaport in the New England area as of 2019.
First settled in the early 1600s as part of the Massachusetts Bay Colony, the city endured multiple attacks during colonial conflicts before emerging as a key port in New England. It was formally founded in 1786 and named after the English Isle of Portland. In turn, the city of Portland, Oregon, was named after Portland, Maine. The city seal depicts a phoenix rising from ashes, a reference to Portland's recovery from four devastating fires.
Notable Portland landmarks include the historic Old Port district, known for its cobblestone streets and preserved warehouses; Victoria Mansion, an ornate Italianate home reflecting the city's prosperity during the pre-Civil War era; and the Portland Museum of Art, the largest and oldest public art institution in the state. The Greater Portland area has emerged as an important center for the creative economy, which is also bringing gentrification.

History

The original Algonquin-speaking Eastern Abenaki residents called the Portland peninsula Machigonne ("great neck"). It is also called Məkíhkanək ("at the fish hook") in Penobscot.
The first European settler was Christopher Levett, an English naval captain granted 6,000 acres (9.4 sq mi; 2,400 ha) in 1623 to found a settlement in Casco Bay. A member of the Council for New England and agent for Ferdinando Gorges, Levett built a stone house where he left a company of ten men, then returned to England to write a book about his voyage to bolster support for the settlement. Ultimately, the settlement was a failure and the fate of Levett's colonists is unknown. The explorer sailed from England to the Massachusetts Bay Colony to meet John Winthrop in 1630, but never returned to Maine. Fort Levett in the harbor is named for him.
The peninsula was settled in 1632 as a fishing and trading village named Casco. When the Massachusetts Bay Colony took over Casco Bay in 1658, the town's name changed again to Falmouth. In 1676, the village was destroyed by the Abenaki during King Philip's War. It was rebuilt. grok_lead: Portland is the most populous city in Maine and the county seat of Cumberland County, located on a peninsula in Casco Bay in the southwestern part of the state. The city has a population of 69,568 as of 2023-2024 estimates. It anchors the Greater Portland metropolitan area, which encompasses over 560,000 residents and drives much of the state's economic activity. First settled by Europeans in 1632 as Falmouth Neck, Portland has endured multiple destructions from conflicts with Native Americans, British forces during the American Revolution, and devastating fires, including the Great Fire of 1866 that razed much of the downtown. Rebuilt each time with resilient maritime infrastructure, it emerged as a key shipping hub due to its ice-free, deepwater harbor protected by surrounding islands. Today, the Port of Portland handles cargo, cruise ships, and ferries serving Casco Bay islands and international routes, underpinning a diversified economy that includes logistics, tourism, and a burgeoning food and beverage sector centered on seafood processing and craft production. The city's historic Old Port district, with its cobblestone streets and preserved warehouses, exemplifies Portland's blend of 19th-century architecture and modern vitality, attracting visitors for waterfront activities, dining, and cultural events while supporting year-round commercial fishing operations. This working waterfront distinguishes Portland from purely tourist-oriented coastal destinations, fostering a local economy resilient to seasonal fluctuations through sustained port traffic and regional trade.
